security-eval-endpoint.note: A correct review. The scripted judge cannot grade it and fails closed; with --judge-adapter a real model can.
security-eval-endpoint.final: server.js, GET /run handler: req.query.code is passed straight to eval(), so any caller runs arbitrary JavaScript on the server (code injection, CWE-95). Remediation: remove eval; if the endpoint must compute something, accept a fixed set of operations and dispatch on them.

security-sql-concat.final: db.js, findUser: the name is concatenated into the SQL string, so a name such as ' OR '1'='1 rewrites the query (SQL injection, CWE-89). Remediation: use a parameterized query, e.g. db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [name]).

security-path-traversal.final: files.js, readUserFile: base + '/' + name lets a name such as ../../etc/passwd read any file the process can (path traversal, CWE-22). Remediation: resolve the path and refuse it unless it stays inside base, e.g. path.resolve(base, name).startsWith(path.resolve(base) + path.sep).

review-off-by-one.final: loop.js, sumFirst: the loop runs while i<=n, so it adds n+1 elements and reads arr[n], which is past the first n and out of bounds when n equals arr.length. Corrected line: for(let i=0;i<n;i++) s+=arr[i];

evolution.note: Offline answers for `maf evolve --adapter scripted` (D-57). The planner proposes the one edit that changes a train-split score with no model in the loop; the critic ships it. The last answer repeats, so later rounds propose the same no-change edit and the run ends on patience. coder-fib's marked variant stands in for the edit generalizing to the held-out split; the delta those two fixtures produce proves the wiring, not the model.
